latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Chikungunya virus is inoculated by Aedes mosquitoes and produces a short high-viremia phase that drives abrupt fever and enables RT-PCR positivity early in illness.
Interferon, IL-6, chemokines, and systemic inflammatory signaling produce high fever, chills, headache, myalgia, malaise, CRP rise, and tachycardia.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Musculoskeletal fibroblast, tendon, and synovial inflammation
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Viral tropism and immune activation in fibroblasts, tendons, periarticular tissue, muscles, and synovium produce severe acute polyarthralgia, arthritis, edema, gait limitation, and chronic post-chikungunya inflammatory arthritis.
Cutaneous vascular and dermal inflammation produces maculopapular rash, erythema, panniculitis, edema, conjunctival hyperemia, and rare severe bullous or hemorrhagic lesions.
Acute arboviral inflammation can produce lymphopenia or leukopenia, mild thrombocytopenia, transaminitis, and rarely clinically important coagulopathy or hepatitis-like organ injury.
After acute infection, a subset of patients develop persistent synovitis, tenosynovitis, pain amplification, rheumatoid-like biomarkers, or chronic inflammatory arthritis lasting months to years.
Chikungunya can cause encephalitis, encephalopathy, myelitis, myeloneuropathy, Guillain-Barre syndrome, seizures, or stroke-like syndromes through direct CNS infection and immune-mediated injury.

High inflammatory burden, comorbidity, pregnancy, extremes of age, dehydration, medication toxicity, or severe atypical disease can produce hypotension, AKI, myocarditis, respiratory failure, coagulopathy, and death.

supportive_care: Keep the disease name pure: Chikungunya. Chronic arthritis, encephalitis, pregnancy, travel, transplant, and severe bullous disease are represented as mechanisms, axes, risk factors, event hazards, and treatment modifiers.

Record onset timing, mosquito or outbreak exposure, travel, local dengue/Zika circulation, fever curve, joint distribution, rash pattern, eye findings, and neurologic symptoms rather than collapsing the case into an arbovirus label.

Use CHIKV RT-PCR early and IgM/paired serology later; pathogen testing is modeled because routine symptoms, vitals, CBC, and liver tests cannot reliably distinguish chikungunya from dengue, Zika, Mayaro, parvovirus, acute HIV, rickettsioses, or bacterial sepsis.
In dengue-endemic areas, avoid NSAIDs until dengue and major bleeding risk are reasonably excluded; use acetaminophen within liver-safe dosing and hydration while awaiting tests.
Monitor CBC with differential, platelets, creatinine, AST/ALT, bilirubin, INR, CK when myositis or AKI is suspected, and CRP/ESR when persistent inflammatory arthritis is present.

Assess severe warning features: hypotension, bleeding, bullous or necrotic skin lesions, reduced consciousness, seizures, focal deficit, dyspnea, renal dysfunction, hepatitis/coagulopathy, myocarditis, pregnancy, neonate, older age, or major comorbidity.

For encephalitis or meningitis presentations, structure CSF cell count and differential, protein, glucose, CHIKV IgM/PCR, MRI pattern, seizure activity, GCS, airway support, and alternative pathogen testing.
There is no routinely proven specific antiviral treatment for chikungunya; acute management is supportive and complication-directed.

Persistent post-chikungunya inflammatory arthritis should be followed longitudinally with function, joint swelling, CRP/ESR, mimic review, and rheumatology-directed anti-inflammatory or DMARD decisions when symptoms persist.
Avoid using response to IVIG, steroids, antibiotics, or NSAIDs as diagnostic truth; treatment response belongs to course evidence or forward simulation context.
distillation_quality_notes: Disease-specific input is only Disease: Chikungunya (id: D-CHIKUNGUNYA).
New disease-specific axes avoid '_or_' compound names; parent findings such as rash_activity, arthralgia_activity, arthritis_activity, and csf_inflammation_activity are separated from satellites.
